resources.string: Discover devices, manage your hotspot and inspect network health
Discover your local network. Manage phone-hotspot clients or start temporary rooted Wi-Fi controls.
Tap Scan to inspect the local Wi-Fi segment. Discovery is incomplete on isolated networks.
This Wi-Fi connection has no supported private IPv4 segment. IPv6-only discovery is not available.
Checking %1$d local addresses… Tap Scan again to stop.
Found %1$d responding devices across %2$d addresses. Silent devices may be missing.
Connect to Wi-Fi for LAN discovery and local interface observations.
Allow local network access to scan. You can still inspect supported hotspot controls.
Only restrictions owned by NetLab appear here. Restoring removes its rule; it cannot override another hotspot allow list or a router policy.
Stop the rooted IPv4 session and send ARP repairs. Remove hotspot restrictions installed by NetLab, preserving unrelated hotspot rules. Remote ARP caches may take time to recover.
No matching devices. Scan Wi-Fi or connect a test device to your phone’s hotspot.
No NetLab restrictions. Everyone is out of Jail.
Restore by %1$s; earlier if the hotspot or controller restarts
Last scan · connection not verified now
This device belongs to the phone hotspot inventory. Pause blocks its Wi-Fi association, including local access, rather than only internet traffic.
This device responded on your connected Wi-Fi. Root Wi-Fi controls can attempt a temporary IPv4 pause or rate cap after a root scan. IPv6 and router protections can bypass or prevent control.
Trust is a label, not authentication. Randomized MACs and reused IP addresses can represent a different device after reconnection.
Disconnect the selected clients from your phone’s hotspot. Rules expire at the chosen time and restore early when the hotspot or controller restarts.
Hotspot client blocking is unavailable. Check Diagnostics for hardware capability and controller status.
Select currently connected hotspot clients for Pause, or NetLab-owned Jail entries for Restore.
Requests accepted: %1$d · failed: %2$d. Check each device’s status.
Passive gateway observations. A changed address may be normal roaming or router configuration; it does not prove an attack.
ARP visibility unavailable. Gateway-route observations remain available; ARP protection is not active.
Gateway neighbour visible · passive observations only
Gateway changed on this connection. Check router settings; confidence: informational.
Gateway MAC changed. Verify roaming or router changes; confidence: unverified.
Live receive/transmit rates on this phone’s Wi-Fi interface. These are local interface counters, not individual peer traffic.
Waiting for the next traffic sample…
The driver did not confirm a disconnect. NetLab removed the unconfirmed restriction.
Apply a timed pause to current hotspot clients, or keep a bandwidth preset for a future supported enforcement backend.
Continuous allow-only lockdown and recurring schedules are unavailable. “Pause current clients” does not block future arrivals.
Off by default. When enabled, keep up to 128 local records for seven days in private encrypted device storage. Names and trust labels are saved when you choose them.
Discovery history cleared. Names and trust labels retained.
Delete NetLab’s local device metadata and turn off history. Use Emergency restore separately to remove hotspot restrictions.
These saved presets do not apply native hotspot caps. Use Root Wi-Fi controls to apply a temporary IPv4 cap to selected devices on your connected Wi-Fi.
Numeric values are kbps. The slider spans 0–100 Mbps; 0 means unlimited.
Preset saved locally. No bandwidth rule was applied.
Capabilities come from the active controller and phone hardware. Unavailable controls are never reported as applied.
Timed rules need alarm access and an idle exemption for Hecker NetLab controller. Session rules remain available without them.
Android tethering offload status: %1$d (-1 means unknown)
Hotspot blocking requires HAL support. Root Wi-Fi controls use a separate temporary IPv4 relay. Router APIs, IPv6 controls and persistent lockdown are unavailable.
The Wi-Fi HAL has not reported support for client blocking. No compatibility override is used.
Reliable restore alarms are unavailable. Timed rules are refused or restored early.
This client already has an external block or allow-list rule. Manage that rule in hotspot settings.
The private rule journal is unavailable. New restrictions are disabled; inspect blocked clients in hotspot settings if recovery cannot finish.
Restoration is pending. NetLab keeps ownership and retries without clearing unrelated rules.
The client or rule changed. Refresh the list before trying again.
The controller could not verify this operation. Inspect the current Jail state and use Emergency restore if needed.
Names and models come from local service advertisements or hotspot DHCP. Device types are hints, not verified identities. Private MAC addresses and silent devices may hide these details.
Root operation ended with an error
Temporarily pause or limit selected devices on Wi-Fi networks you administer. Uses root and ARP to relay selected IPv4 traffic through this phone.

IPv4 gateway traffic only. Devices stay connected to Wi-Fi; IPv6 and direct local traffic continue. Client isolation and ARP protection may prevent control. The phone must stay online and awake. No automatic restart. Stop sends ARP repairs; remote caches may take time to recover.
Root is requested only when you press Check or Scan.
Root granted · ready for an explicit action
Session started · waiting for selected IPv4 traffic
Selected IPv4 traffic relayed with rate caps
%1$d devices from root scan on this connection
Run a root Wi-Fi scan on this connection first.
Select 1–32 devices from the root scan.
Duration: 1–3,600 seconds. Rates are kbps per direction, per device; 0 leaves that direction unlimited. At least one cap is required. Short packet bursts are possible.
Enter 0–1,024,000 kbps, with at least one nonzero cap
Request queued. Check the session status.
Session bytes · forwarded ↑ %1$d / ↓ %2$d · dropped ↑ %3$d / ↓ %4$d. Only packets handled by this relay are counted.
Root or raw-packet access was denied, or the helper is missing. Check the KernelSU grant for Hecker NetLab controller. SELinux stays enforcing.
A peer is unreachable or its MAC changed. Scan again before starting.
The selected private IPv4 Wi-Fi route is unavailable or changed. Stop VPN/tethering conflicts and scan the current connection again.
Kernel forwarding is already enabled and could bypass the caps. Stop hotspot/tethering first. NetLab does not change global forwarding settings.
Enable controller notifications so Stop and restore remains accessible.
A root operation is running. Stop it before starting another.
The original Wi-Fi link was lost. ARP repairs could not be sent there; affected devices may need to reconnect or wait for their cache to expire.
The root operation did not complete. Check the connection, scan again, or use Stop and restore.
